verdict.rationale: HMRC's own guidance says an agent can act for the taxpayer: an agent can sign a client up for Making Tax Digital, and agents have their own sign-up path and client-authorisation request links. That is only a glancing mention of delegated access, not a published scope of what a third party may and may not do. Missing for 10: named authorisation forms, defined agent roles and permission levels, a list of actions or signatures that must stay personal to the taxpayer, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, exactly what a third party may and may not do on my behalf is published — the authorization forms, the roles, and which signatures stay personal

citations.quote: If you use an agent, they can sign you up instead.
agents hold their own sign-up path and client-authorisation request links.
